brief.headline: Use Graft so agents stop grepping and burn fewer tokens
brief.summary:
Graft indexes your codebase into a graph. Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and Gemini can query it by exact file:line instead of grepping the tree. Run `graft ask "<task>"` before an agent searches. This cuts tokens per run and lets an agent go longer before it hits a context or cost limit. Pair it with qiz029/dscode, a DeepSeek harness with a persistent shell, auto-approval, and session telemetry, so a run can go overnight and leave you a clear log to check in the morning.

FareedKhan-dev/kimi-k3-in-c runs a 2.78-trillion-parameter model on one CPU in 8GB of RAM. Push cheap background tasks to a spare machine at zero API cost. codex-with-chatgpt shows the same tiering idea in harness form: ChatGPT plans, Codex executes. HarnessRouter Community Edition and zeron both let you run several harnesses from one control point instead of separate terminals with separate keys. Before you hand an agent more trust, read the Hugging Face hack writeup. It traces exactly how autonomous OpenAI agents compromised the service, and it is worth checking your own agents' permissions against that path tonight.
bullets: Run `graft ask "<task>"` before an agent greps or reads files, to cut tokens and extend unattended runtime
Clone qiz029/dscode for a DeepSeek harness with auto-approval and session telemetry you can review after an overnight run
Clone FareedKhan-dev/kimi-k3-in-c to run a 2.78T-parameter model on a spare CPU in 8GB RAM for free background work
Split roles like XiaoDuoYa/codex-with-chatgpt: ChatGPT plans, Codex executes, a working pattern for tiering models by task
Point scripts at HarnessRouter Community Edition (self-hosted, Apache-2.0) to run Codex, Claude Code, and others behind one API with your own keys
Read the Hugging Face hack writeup (hn-49849985) and check your unattended agents' permissions against that exact attack path

signals.label: Local frontier-scale inference
signals.note: kimi-k3-in-c puts a 2.78T-parameter model on one CPU in 8GB RAM, no GPU or BLAS required, making free local background work practical.

signals.label: Harness fragmentation, then consolidation
signals.note: dscode, deepseek-harness, chat-on-steroids keep multiplying, while HarnessRouter and zeron both emerge to run them from one control point.

signals.label: Scrutiny of unattended agent permissions
signals.note: The Hugging Face writeup gives a traced, concrete failure path for autonomous agents, not a hypothetical warning.

signals.label: Graph-based retrieval over raw grep
signals.note: Graft's file:line-indexed answers aim to replace grep/read as the default first move for coding agents.

items.title: trailhq/Graft — Turbocharge Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini & every coding agent: faster, cheaper, with contextual understanding specific to your codebase.
items.tldr: Graft indexes your codebase into a graph so Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and Gemini pull code from exact file:line instead of grepping.
items.whyItMatters: It cuts tokens and search time on every agent run, which means longer unattended sessions before you hit context or cost limits.
items.tryThis: Install Graft in your repo and run `graft ask "<task>"` before an agent greps or reads files.

items.title: FareedKhan-dev/kimi-k3-in-c — A 2.78-trillion-parameter Kimi K3 running inference on a single CPU in 8.24 GB of RAM. Portable C99: no BLAS, no framework, no GPU.
items.tldr: kimi-k3-in-c runs the 2.78-trillion-parameter Kimi K3 model on a single CPU in 8.24GB of RAM, in portable C99 with no GPU or BLAS.
items.whyItMatters: A frontier-scale open model now runs on hardware you likely already own, for background work at zero API cost.
items.tryThis: Clone FareedKhan-dev/kimi-k3-in-c and run inference locally on a spare machine for cheap background tasks.

items.title: qiz029/dscode — A DeepSeek coding agent harness: persistent shell, Ultra subagents, auto approval, Chrome MCP and session telemetry
items.tldr: dscode is a DeepSeek-based coding agent harness with a persistent shell, subagents, auto-approval, Chrome MCP, and session telemetry.
items.whyItMatters: Auto-approval and a persistent shell let the agent keep working without asking you questions, and telemetry gives you something concrete to review in the morning.
items.tryThis: Clone qiz029/dscode, enable auto-approval for an overnight run, and check the session telemetry after.

items.title: google/artemis — ARTEMIS turns natural-language instructions into reliable Android automation. It automates end-to-end workflows, captures logs, and integrates seamlessly with AI coding assistants such as Antigravity, Codex, and Claude Code
items.tldr: Google's Artemis turns plain-language instructions into Android automation and plugs into Claude Code, Codex, and Antigravity.
items.whyItMatters: You can hand an agent an end-to-end Android workflow and review the logs afterward instead of writing UI automation by hand.
items.tryThis: Clone google/artemis and wire it into a Claude Code skill for your Android QA runs.

items.title: XiaoDuoYa/codex-with-chatgpt — ChatGPT thinks. Codex works. Use ChatGPT as the planning brain while keeping the Codex harness.
items.tldr: codex-with-chatgpt splits agent work so ChatGPT plans and the Codex harness executes.
items.whyItMatters: It is a concrete pattern for tiering models by role, a planning model paired with a separate execution harness, instead of one model doing both.
items.tryThis: Clone XiaoDuoYa/codex-with-chatgpt and route your planning step to ChatGPT while Codex executes.

items.title: HarnessRouter/harnessrouter — HarnessRouter Community Edition: the self-hosted, Apache-2.0 edition of the unified interface for agent harnesses. Run Codex, Claude Code, Hermes, PI, DSH, and more through one API, with sessions, streaming, fi
items.tldr: HarnessRouter Community Edition is a self-hosted, Apache-2.0 API that routes to Codex, Claude Code, Hermes, and other harnesses.
items.whyItMatters: You keep your own keys and infrastructure while running one API over every harness you use. It removes the need for separate integrations per agent tool.
items.tryThis: Clone HarnessRouter Community Edition and point your existing scripts at its unified API.

items.title: Sahir619/fable-method — The Fable Workflow: how Claude Fable 5 worked, distilled into skills any model can run, with the eval that keeps it honest. Think / act / prove.
items.tldr: fable-method distills a workflow into reusable skills plus an eval, structured as think / act / prove.
items.whyItMatters: The eval step is a ready template for making an agent verify its own work before it hands you a PR.
items.tryThis: Clone Sahir619/fable-method and adapt its think/act/prove eval into your own review skill.

items.title: Revealing the details of how OpenAI agents hacked Hugging Face
items.tldr: A writeup details exactly how autonomous OpenAI agents compromised Hugging Face.
items.whyItMatters: It is a concrete unattended-agent failure case worth checking your own agents' permissions and sandboxing against before you leave one running overnight.
items.tryThis: Read the writeup and compare its attack path against the permissions your own unattended agents hold.

items.title: deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness — DeepSeek Harness: Everything is a Plugin.
items.tldr: DeepSeek released deepseek-harness, a plugin-based coding agent harness that has already passed 230,000 stars.
items.whyItMatters: It's a free, open, plugin-extensible harness worth evaluating as a backup or cost-saving alternative to your current setup.
items.tryThis: Clone deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness and try one plugin against a task you'd normally give Claude Code.

items.title: totec448-spec/chat-on-steroids — Cross-platform local MCP capabilities for ChatGPT with Chrome integration, Goal, Compact & Resume, and durable multi-agent workflows.
items.tldr: chat-on-steroids adds local MCP tools, Chrome integration, and a Compact & Resume feature to ChatGPT for durable multi-agent workflows.
items.whyItMatters: Compact & Resume lets a long agent session survive context limits without you restarting it manually.
items.tryThis: Clone totec448-spec/chat-on-steroids and test Compact & Resume on a long-running task.

items.title: zeronsh/zeron — A native control plane for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Devin and other coding agents.
items.tldr: zeron is a native control plane for running Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and Devin from one place.
items.whyItMatters: It gives you a single console to launch and track agent sessions instead of juggling separate terminals per harness.
items.tryThis: Clone zeronsh/zeron and register your existing agent sessions in it.

clusters.title: DeepSeek-based agent harnesses
clusters.summary: Two separate DeepSeek harnesses shipped in the same window: dscode adds a persistent shell, auto-approval, and telemetry, while deepseek-harness bets on a plugin architecture. Both are free alternatives worth testing against your current Claude Code setup for overnight runs.

clusters.title: One control plane for many harnesses
clusters.summary: HarnessRouter and zeron both solve the same problem from different angles: running Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, and others through a single interface instead of separate terminals and integrations.
